query: For high-entropy alloys intended for harsh corrosive mechanical environments, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion, and why? Propose a controlled comparison that would test the hypothesis, predict how combined degradation and its wear and corrosion components would differ from a matched baseline, define where the prediction should hold or fail, identify supporting prior evidence, and state an observation that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: In multiprincipal-element (high-entropy) alloys, simultaneous resistance to aqueous corrosion and sliding wear is governed primarily by the ability to form and mechanically retain an ultrathin, Cr–Al–rich nanocrystalline oxide/spinel tribofilm that (i) passivates the surface electrochemically and (ii) lowers friction and ploughing by acting as a mechanically hard, lubricious layer; alloys that can dynamically regenerate this mixed Cr₂O₃–Al₂O₃/(Cr,Al)₃O₄ tribofilm under tribocorrosion will exhibit substantially lower combined material loss than otherwise-similar alloys that cannot.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase face-centred-cubic (FCC) high-entropy alloy CoCrFeNi (cast, homogenised, grain size ≈ 20–30 µm).
generation.intervention: Add 10 at.% Al (CoCrFeNiAl0.5) to increase the Cr+Al activity above the threshold for forming a continuous Cr–Al mixed oxide during sliding in chloride solution.
generation.conditions: Room temperature, aerated 3.5 wt % NaCl, open-circuit potential, reciprocating ball-on-disk sliding (5 N normal load, 5 Hz, 10 000 cycles, alumina ball counter-body).
generation.structural_mediator: In-situ-generated, ≈10–50 nm thick Cr₂O₃/Al₂O₃ + (Cr,Al)₃O₄ nanocomposite tribofilm adherent to the alloy surface inside the wear track.
generation.mechanism: Frictional flash heating and plastic shear locally enhance outward diffusion of Cr and Al; rapid oxidation produces a dense nanocomposite oxide that (a) blocks chloride-induced metal dissolution (lowering corrosion current) and (b) provides a hard, low-shear interface that reduces abrasive and adhesive wear. Because the layer is constantly replenished by continued diffusion, it self-heals after micro-fracture, sustaining protection during sliding.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the baseline CoCrFeNi, the Al-containing CoCrFeNiAl0.5 alloy will show: • ≥50 % lower total mass (volume) loss in tribocorrosion. • ~40 % lower wear volume (mechanical component) after cathodic protection that suppresses corrosion. • ≥1 order-of-magnitude lower corrosion current density inside the wear track during sliding-wear-free potential holds. Synergy term (ΔW − Wwear − Wcorr) will be markedly smaller for the Al-added alloy.
generation.baseline: Same experimental protocol applied to the Cr-rich but Al-free CoCrFeNi alloy, which forms a less protective, mechanically fragile Cr-hydroxide film that is repeatedly removed, giving higher wear and corrosion rates.
generation.boundary: Prediction should hold for neutral to mildly alkaline, aerated chloride media at ≤100 °C and sliding speeds/loads that generate sufficient flash temperature (<200 °C) but not catastrophic delamination. It may fail (a) in deaerated acid (pH<2) where passive films dissolve, (b) at ≥300 °C where oxide spallation dominates, or (c) under impact/rolling contact where film retention differs.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of the wear-reduction factor (50 %) is estimated; actual value may vary with counter-body material, load, and alloy microstructure. Role of other elements (Mo, Nb) is not accounted for. Possible complex interactions between oxide toughness and chloride infiltration are not fully resolved.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two alloys: CoCrFeNi (baseline) and CoCrFeNiAl0.5 (intervention). After identical solution heat treatment, perform tribocorrosion tests in 3.5 % NaCl as specified. Measure (i) open circuit potential during sliding, (ii) potentiostatic current transients at +0.1 V_SCE with and without sliding, (iii) wear track profiles (3D profilometry) for volume loss, and (iv) post-test surface/tribofilm chemistry and thickness by TEM and XPS.
measurements: Wear volume under cathodic protection (pure wear)
Electrochemical current density during sliding-free holds (pure corrosion)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al-containing alloy does NOT show (a) ≥20 % lower total tribocorrosion loss AND (b) a continuous Cr–Al oxide tribofilm, OR if its synergy term exceeds that of the Al-free alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.
